how: Read by hand from each county’s budget PDF as filed with the Idaho State Controller (Transparent Idaho). Scanned filings were read with text recognition and corrected using their own column totals. Every fund and department carries the PDF page it came from; funds are summed and compared with the total the county reported to the Controller.

16001.title: FY2024-2025 Ada County Adopted Budget, 'Budget Request by Fund Type' (document page 9)

funds.name: District Court (Clerk and Trial Court Administration)

notes: This is the county's adopted FY2025 budget book. The summary table on document page 9 (PDF page 19) lists each fund type, its funds and departments. Every amount here is from that table; the page lists no other level of detail.

The book's all-funds total is $390,880,245. It includes three special taxing districts that have their own levies: Emergency Medical Services ($26,043,647), Pest Extermination ($991,336) and Mosquito Abatement ($1,825,251), which together are $28,860,234. They are left out here because they are separate districts, not county funds.

The book groups funds as General Fund, Special Levy Funds, Self-Supported Special Revenue Funds, Special Taxing Districts, and Self-Supported Business-Type Funds. The list here shows each fund by name. Clerk of the Court and Trial Court Administrator are the District Court special levy fund, as described on page 12 of the PDF.
Public Defender is shown inside the General Fund as the book prints it. The book says the public defender's office was moving to the State of Idaho.
corrections: The text of the summary table came out with names and numbers on different lines. Each amount was matched to its name using the program-type table on the next page and by checking that the department amounts add to the printed fund totals.
16001.controller_note: The adopted budget's all-funds total is $390,880,245. The State Controller's figure is $362,020,011. The difference is exactly $28,860,234, the combined budget of the three special taxing districts (Emergency Medical Services, Pest Extermination and Mosquito Abatement) printed in the same table. They are left out of this page.

16003.title: Notice of Public Hearing, Adams County FY2025 tentative budget (budget hearing August 26, 2024)
notes: Amounts are the "Tentative Budget FY ending 9/30/2025" Total column in the Notice of Public Hearing (hearing August 26, 2024). The notice's own grand total is $14,869,093.34; funds here are rounded to whole dollars.

The notice also lists funds with $0 budgeted for 2025 (Grant - Weed BLM, Grant - Public Defense, Sheriff donations, Juvenile Trust, Solid Waste Foreclosure, Old Courthouse Landscape, Unclaimed Property); they are left out.
Page 1 of the PDF is a separate worksheet that shows a higher total ($16.5 million) from an earlier update; the budget here follows the published notice, which matches the Controller figure.
Fund 911 has no readable label in the notice; it is listed as "911" from the revenue page.
corrections: OCR garbled most of the amounts on page 3 and 4; every figure was read from the page image and checked: Justice fund departments add to 3,094,221, and fund totals add to the notice grand total 14,869,093.34.

16005.title: Public notice of budget hearing, August 27, 2024 (FY2025 proposed expenditures; published Aug 2, 2024)
notes: This is the proposed budget printed in the notice for the August 27, 2024 hearing. The file has no later adopted version.
Amounts are the 'FY 2025 Proposed Expenditures' Total column. The notice also shows salary and other-expense splits, prior-year spending, and revenue; those are not used here.

The notice lists an Ambulance District ($5,199,686, marked with an asterisk; the footnote is not in this file). It is left out because it appears to be a separate district, not part of the county's own funds. With it, the notice's total is $103,763,209.
In the notice, Fair Exhibit is the three lines Fair Exhibit, County Fair and 4-H; Park and Recreation and Road and Bridge show one working line each.
16005.controller_note: The notice’s grand total is $103,763,209. Without the Ambulance District ($5,199,686) it is $98,563,523. The documents do not say why the Controller’s figure is lower.

16007.title: Bear Lake County FY2024 final approved budget (one-page summary by fund)
notes: This PDF is one page: a summary table of the "Proposed Budget" column by fund, marked by hand "2024 Final Approved Budget". The sheet is headed "County Revenues - Budgeted"; the county balances each fund, so the budget column is used as the amount for each fund. The page is printed sideways.
Funds with $0 (Road and Bridge Capital, and the "65-1305 Levy" line) are left out. No departments are listed.
The county total is $13,298,083 and the ARPA Recovery Funds line adds $1,198,033, for a grand total of $14,496,116, which equals the Controller figure.
corrections: The OCR text was empty; all numbers were read from the page image. The fund lines add to the sheet's grand total of 14,496,116.

notes: Amounts are the "Approved Amount" column of the county's Budget Totals (expenditure) report for the "2025 Approved Budget."
The Pest fund shows $3,500 in the Budget Officer column but no approved amount, so it is left out.
The report lists departments only inside Current Expense and the Justice Fund; other funds have one line.
The report includes the ARPA Fund Projects ($354,010).
corrections: OCR dropped digits in several rows (Solid Waste, General Road, Justice Fund Sheriff). All figures were read from the page images and the approved column adds to the report grand total of 15,744,647.

The report also shows what each office asked for ($41,237,970 in total) and the budget officer's figure. Those are not used here.
Funds with one department of the same name are shown without a department list.

The Waterways fund is maintenance ($36,118) plus the boat patrol grant ($21,314).
The Jail amount was blank in the OCR text and was read from the page image. Its figure also makes the General Fund departments add to the fund total.
corrections: OCR left the Jail line blank; the page image shows 4,200,396, which is also what the General Fund total requires.

The resolution text (page 1) says the final budget is $19,264,128; both attachments add to $19,254,128.17, which is also the Controller figure. The attachment figures are used. The Grant Fund line is blank for 2025 and is left out.
The Capital Projects line in Current Expense ($2,247,080) is the largest single line in that fund; the notice does not explain it.
corrections: OCR of pages 2 and 3 was unreadable (rotated tables). All figures were read from the page images; each fund's departments add to its fund total and the funds add to the 19,254,128.17 grand total.
